mcqs.question: A molecule is chiral when it:
options: Is not superimposable on its mirror image
Has an alternating axis of symmetry
mcqs.explanation: Chirality means non-superimposability on the mirror image; any σ, i or Sn makes a molecule achiral.

mcqs.question: In the formula [α] = α/(l × c), the tube length l is expressed in:
mcqs.explanation: Specific rotation uses the tube length in dm and concentration in g/mL.

mcqs.question: How many stereoisomers does tartaric acid have?
mcqs.explanation: Two similar stereocentres give (+), (−) and meso; the meso form makes it 3, not 2^2 = 4.

mcqs.question: A meso compound is optically inactive because of:
mcqs.explanation: An internal plane of symmetry makes one half cancel the rotation of the other.

mcqs.question: According to the CIP sequence rules, which group has the highest priority?
mcqs.explanation: Priority goes first by the atomic number of the attached atom; O (in –OH) beats C in the other three.

mcqs.question: D-Glyceraldehyde has which absolute configuration?
mcqs.explanation: With OH > CHO > CH2OH > H, D-glyceraldehyde works out as (R).

mcqs.question: An SN2 reaction at a stereocentre takes place with:
mcqs.explanation: Backside attack turns the molecule inside out (Walden inversion).

mcqs.question: Brucine and strychnine are used in the resolution of racemic:
mcqs.explanation: These optically active bases form diastereomeric salts with racemic acids.

mcqs.question: Pasteur separated the enantiomers of sodium ammonium tartrate by:
mcqs.explanation: He picked out mirror-image crystals by hand under a lens.

mcqs.question: Asymmetric synthesis using circularly polarised light without any chiral compound is called:
mcqs.explanation: Absolute asymmetric synthesis relies only on a physical chiral influence.

mcqs.question: Which compound shows geometrical isomerism?
mcqs.explanation: 2-Butene has two different groups on each doubly bonded carbon; the others have two H or two CH3 on one carbon.

mcqs.question: Maleic acid forms an anhydride on heating but fumaric acid does not because maleic acid is the:
mcqs.explanation: Only in the cis isomer are the two –COOH groups close enough to lose water and form a ring.

mcqs.question: In the E–Z system, Z means that the higher-priority groups are:
mcqs.explanation: Z (zusammen) = together; E (entgegen) = opposite.

mcqs.question: Syn hydroxylation of maleic acid with cold dilute alkaline KMnO4 gives:
mcqs.explanation: Syn addition to the cis acid gives the meso diol; fumaric acid gives the racemate.

mcqs.question: The most stable conformation of n-butane is:
mcqs.explanation: In the anti form the two methyl groups are 180° apart, with no steric or torsional strain.

mcqs.question: The most stable conformation of cyclohexane is:
mcqs.explanation: The chair has no angle strain and all bonds are staggered.

mcqs.question: A methyl group on cyclohexane prefers the equatorial position mainly to avoid:
mcqs.explanation: An axial group clashes with the axial hydrogens on C-3 and C-5.

mcqs.question: Optical activity in a biphenyl requires bulky ortho groups and:
options: Free rotation about the central bond
mcqs.explanation: If either ring has identical ortho groups, a plane of symmetry removes chirality.

mcqs.question: Addition of bromine to trans-2-butene gives:
mcqs.explanation: Anti addition to the trans alkene gives the meso product; cis gives the racemate.

mcqs.question: The C–H out-of-plane bending band near 965 cm⁻¹ in the IR spectrum indicates a:
mcqs.explanation: trans-CH=CH– absorbs strongly near 965 cm⁻¹; cis absorbs at lower frequency.

mcqs.question: The order of aromaticity is:
mcqs.explanation: Resonance energies fall in this order (about 150, 122, 88 and 67 kJ/mol).

mcqs.question: Electrophilic substitution in pyrrole occurs mainly at:
mcqs.explanation: Attack at C-2 gives an intermediate with three resonance structures.

mcqs.question: Pyrrole is a very weak base because its nitrogen lone pair:
options: Is part of the aromatic sextet
mcqs.explanation: Protonating N would destroy aromaticity, so pyrrole protonates at C-2 instead.

mcqs.question: 1,4-Dicarbonyl compounds heated with ammonia give pyrroles. This is the:
mcqs.explanation: Paal–Knorr uses NH3 for pyrroles, acid for furans and P2S5 for thiophenes.

mcqs.question: Furan is obtained industrially from:
mcqs.explanation: Pentosans give furfural with dilute acid; furfural is decarbonylated to furan.

mcqs.question: Thiophene is removed from coal-tar benzene by shaking with:
mcqs.explanation: Thiophene sulphonates much faster than benzene and dissolves in the acid layer.

mcqs.question: Which ring takes part most readily in Diels–Alder reactions as a diene?
mcqs.explanation: Furan has the lowest aromaticity, so it behaves most like a diene.

mcqs.question: The Hantzsch–Widman name of a saturated five-membered ring containing one oxygen is:
mcqs.explanation: -olane is the saturated five-membered stem without N; oxolane is tetrahydrofuran.

mcqs.question: Raney nickel desulphurisation of thiophene gives:
mcqs.explanation: Raney Ni removes sulphur and saturates the chain.

mcqs.question: Nitrofurantoin, a urinary antiseptic, contains which ring?
mcqs.explanation: It is a 5-nitrofuran derivative.

mcqs.question: Pyridine undergoes electrophilic substitution mainly at:
mcqs.explanation: Attack at C-2 or C-4 would put positive charge on the electronegative nitrogen.

mcqs.question: Heating pyridine with sodium amide gives 2-aminopyridine. This is the:
mcqs.explanation: A nucleophilic amination at C-2 of the π-deficient ring.

mcqs.question: Which is the strongest base?
mcqs.explanation: Piperidine has an sp3 nitrogen (pKa about 11); pyridine about 5.2, aniline 4.6, pyrrole far lower.

mcqs.question: Aniline, glycerol, conc. H2SO4 and nitrobenzene react to give:
mcqs.explanation: This is the Skraup synthesis; glycerol forms acrolein and nitrobenzene is the oxidant.

mcqs.question: Indole undergoes electrophilic substitution mainly at:
mcqs.explanation: C-3 attack lets nitrogen stabilise the cation without disturbing the benzene ring.

mcqs.question: Cyclisation of an N-acyl-β-phenylethylamine with POCl3 gives a 3,4-dihydroisoquinoline. This is the:
mcqs.explanation: Dehydrogenation of the product then gives the isoquinoline.

mcqs.question: Diethyl malonate condenses with urea in the presence of sodium ethoxide to give:
mcqs.explanation: This is the principal pyrimidine synthesis; barbituric acid is pyrimidine-2,4,6-trione.

mcqs.question: The Traube synthesis of purines uses a 4,5-diaminopyrimidine and:
mcqs.explanation: Formic acid provides C-8 and closes the imidazole ring.

mcqs.question: Thiamine (vitamin B1) contains a pyrimidine ring joined to a:
mcqs.explanation: The thiazolium C-2 is the active site of thiamine pyrophosphate.

mcqs.question: The most reactive position of acridine towards nucleophiles is:
mcqs.explanation: C-9, opposite the nitrogen, is the site of amination and chloride exchange.

mcqs.question: Clemmensen reduction uses:
mcqs.explanation: Zn–Hg/HCl reduces C=O to CH2 under acidic conditions.

mcqs.question: Which reagent reduces an ester to a primary alcohol?
mcqs.explanation: NaBH4 is normally too mild for esters; LiAlH4 reduces them.

mcqs.question: The Huang-Minlon modification is associated with the:
mcqs.explanation: It uses hydrazine hydrate and KOH in diethylene glycol in one pot.

mcqs.question: Birch reduction of benzene gives:
mcqs.explanation: Protonation of the cyclohexadienyl anion at its centre gives the non-conjugated 1,4-diene.

mcqs.question: In the Beckmann rearrangement the group that migrates is the one:
options: Of larger size regardless of position
mcqs.explanation: Migration and loss of water are concerted, so only the anti group can move.

mcqs.question: Beckmann rearrangement of cyclohexanone oxime gives:
mcqs.explanation: Ring expansion gives the seven-membered lactam used for nylon-6.

mcqs.question: Oppenauer oxidation uses aluminium tert-butoxide with excess:
mcqs.explanation: Acetone accepts the hydride; it is the reverse of MPV reduction.

mcqs.question: Salicylaldehyde treated with alkaline hydrogen peroxide gives:
mcqs.explanation: The Dakin reaction replaces –CHO by –OH when an o/p-OH is present.

mcqs.question: In the Schmidt reaction a carboxylic acid is converted into:
options: An amide with the same carbons
An amine with one carbon fewer
A nitrile with one carbon more
mcqs.explanation: HN3/H2SO4 converts RCOOH to RNH2 + CO2 + N2 via an isocyanate.

mcqs.question: Benzaldehyde and acetophenone condense in dilute NaOH to give:
mcqs.explanation: Claisen–Schmidt condensation gives benzylideneacetophenone (chalcone).
